title: 🇫🇷 French police dismantle a gang that hacked gold and crypto brokers — then knocked on victims' doors!
body: 🇫🇷 French police dismantle a gang that hacked gold and crypto brokers — then knocked on victims' doors!

French police arrested ten people in a wide fraud case that began with hacking the systems of three precious-metals brokerage firms and a company that helps people declare their crypto holdings for tax purposes.

According to the authorities, the scammers used the stolen customer lists to target victims precisely: "callers" would phone the victim and convince them their data had leaked and that they must move their money or gold to a "safe" place, then others would appear at their front door to collect the gold.
More than 175 gendarmes took part in the raids in Marseille, Lille, Toulouse, Colmar and Paris. The ten suspects were referred to the judiciary on Thursday, and four of them remain in custody.

The most important lesson of this case is that the call warning you about a data leak and asking you to move your money is itself the scam: no official body or bank asks you to move your gold or money by phone, or hand it to a person at your front door.

Simply put: they hacked the brokers to steal customer lists, then called the victims posing as "saviours" to take their gold with their own hands. If someone calls you warning of a leak and asking you to move your money, know that the caller is the scammer.
Has a scammer ever called you claiming to protect your money?
